question: A current of 0.2 A is maintained in a resistor of 10 Ω. The heat produced in the resistor in 1 second is:
solution:
The correct answer is __**0.4 J**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The heat produced (H) in a resistor can be calculated using the formula: **H = I²Rt**, where I is the current, R is the resistance, and t is the time.
 
• Given: Current (I) = **0.2 A**, Resistance (R) = **10 Ω**, Time (t) = **1 second**.
 
• Substituting the given values into the formula: **H = (0.2)² × 10 × 1 = 0.04 × 10 = 0.4 J**.
 
• Therefore, the heat produced in the resistor in 1 second is **0.4 J**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The formula **H = I²Rt** is derived from **Joule's law of heating**, which states that the heat produced in a resistor is proportional to the square of the current, the resistance, and the time for which the current flows.
 
• This principle is widely used in electrical heating appliances such as **electric heaters, toasters, and irons**.
 
• Understanding this concept is fundamental in the field of electrical engineering and physics.
